what_happened: The job was meant to rewrite owner decision cards so they lead with a yes/no question and the outcomes of each answer. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict, saying the reading misread the request. No acceptance criteria or checks are listed as unmet or failed. There were four major findings. (1) The "question" is the old title with "Go ahead with this:" in front, so the card still leads with the text the owner called unclear. (2) The "If yes" and "If no" lines are identical fixed text on every card, so they say nothing about the decision. (3) "Recommend no" is given for every proposal above the raising role's limit, which turns "you must decide this" into invented advice against it. (4) The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met.
cause: The accepted reading described the card's form (a question line, an if-yes line, an if-no line, a recommendation) rather than the quality the owner asked for: a question that is clear in plain words, and outcomes specific to each decision. Presence-style criteria are satisfied by a prefix and fixed strings, so the build passes while the card is as unclear as before. Nothing at the reading or plan stage asks that card text vary with the proposal or be checked against real proposals. Nothing blocks invented content, such as a recommendation the data does not support. The same renderer area was rejected the same way in the previous job (20261103-074940-hcey), and the lesson was not carried into the reading.
prevention: Add a test, required by the reading for any rendered owner-facing text, that builds cards from at least two real or realistic Steward proposals with different content. It must assert three things. The question line is not the title with a fixed prefix. The if-yes and if-no lines differ between proposals and contain proposal-specific facts. Any recommendation is derived from a recorded field, and a card with no recorded recommendation shows none. The critic should reject readings whose criteria only name the card's parts without these behavior checks.
proposed_request: Rewrite the owner decision cards produced by `xtask site` so each card reads clearly to the owner. Each card must lead with a plain-words yes/no question that says what Athena would do if the owner says yes. It is not the proposal title with a prefix. Under it, show an "If yes" line and an "If no" line, each written from that proposal's own recorded fields (its change, cost, risk and source), so two different proposals never show the same outcome text. Show a recommendation only when the proposal's record states one. Do not invent advice, and do not add "Recommend no" just because a proposal is above the raising role's limit. In that case say the owner must decide. Acceptance: (1) a test in xtask builds cards from at least two proposals taken from real Steward proposal shapes, which differ in title, change, cost and risk, and asserts that the question lines, the if-yes lines and the if-no lines all differ and that none is the title plus a fixed prefix; (2) a test shows a proposal with no recorded recommendation renders none and an over-limit proposal renders "you must decide"; (3) `cargo test --workspace`, clippy and `cargo fmt --check` pass; (4) the changelog has an entry.
